design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 01 step 1 « ACCUEIL DE L'APP » : « Mes livres » + a grid of book cards, the dashed accent card creating a book. Component anatomy + tokens from the design system (styles.css): card = surfaces/Card, delete = forms/IconButton (danger), confirmation = surfaces/Modal over a scrim with an error-toned confirm. Low-fi wireframe fidelity, light theme only.

plan.goal: Let an author see all their books on the home screen and open or delete any of them, so the library is the entry point to every existing book (not just freshly created ones).
acceptance_criteria: The home screen lists every persisted book (BookService.listBooks) as a grid of cards, newest first; each card shows the book title and a screen count.
Clicking a book card opens it (BookService.openBook -> book:opened) and navigates to its editor, in that order, after the read resolves.
Each card exposes a delete affordance; deleting is a dangerous action gated behind a confirmation dialog that names the book, warns the deletion is permanent, and offers a labelled « Annuler ».
Confirming deletion removes the book via BookService.deleteBook (persist-remove then book:deleted, in that order) and the card disappears from the live list; cancelling leaves the book intact.
The book list is a live VIEW over BookService (useBooks), recomputed only on book:created / book:deleted, never a private mirror (KR-020/013).
The create affordance (« + Nouveau livre », owned by book-creation) is always present in the grid — including when there is no book — so the empty state still invites action.
book-creation and book-library never import each other: the app root composes LibraryScreen with the create affordance passed as a prop.
The screen renders strictly from design-system tokens/components (Card, IconButton, Modal), light theme; the confirm button is error-toned for the dangerous action; >=44px hit targets.
plan.walking_skeleton: LibraryScreen (the home route) lists books from useBooks() as a grid of BookCards. Clicking a card calls openBook + Router.navigate to the editor. A card's ✕ opens a DeleteBookDialog (confirmation); confirming calls BookService.deleteBook, which persists the removal then emits book:deleted, and the live list drops the card. The create affordance (CreateBookEntry from book-creation) is composed in by App as a prop. Wired entirely through brain.

iterations.goal: Card content & affordances: richer per-book meta (updatedAt, edge/end counts), hover-reveal delete, rename, duplicate; full DS card fidelity matching the wireframe grid.
List ergonomics: search/filter, sort (recent/alpha), and an explicit empty state illustration; guard deleting the currently-open book (navigate home, avoid a dangling editor route).
Cloud-first: reflect sync:status per book, reconcile the list with CloudSyncService, and queue deletes when offline. Deferred until the cloud-sync feature lands.

known_risks: KR-070 — Deleting a book is a dangerous, irreversible action: always gate behind a confirmation dialog (name the book, error-toned confirm, labelled Annuler) and route the delete through BookService.deleteBook (persist-remove then book:deleted, KR-004) — never a raw removal.

KR-071 — The library list is a VIEW over BookService via useBooks (recomputed only on book:created/book:deleted), never a private copy (re-asserts KR-020/013); deleting the currently-open book could leave the editor on a dangling route — guarded in iteration 2.
KR-072 — book-creation and book-library compose at the app root (LibraryScreen receives the create affordance as a prop); neither imports the other (feature isolation).
KR-004 — book:opened/book:deleted fire only AFTER the persistence read/removal resolves, in order; listeners always observe a consistent store.
KR-011 — No raw window.localStorage; list and delete go through PersistenceService via BookService only.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: New brain useBooks() view hook: a cached snapshot recomputed only on book:created/book:deleted via useSyncExternalStore, mirroring useOpenBook — a live VIEW over BookService, not a useEffect mirror (KR-020/013/071).
BookService.deleteBook persists the removal (PersistenceService.remove) before emitting book:deleted, so the list re-reads a store without the book (KR-004/070).
book-creation refactored: the create affordance extracted into CreateBookEntry (button + dialog), decoupled from page chrome; the home chrome + book list now belong to book-library's LibraryScreen.
App composes LibraryScreen with <CreateBookEntry/> as the createEntry prop, so the two features never import each other (KR-072).

Deletion gated behind DeleteBookDialog; the pending-deletion target is local UI state (not derived from props, KR-013). Reused the shared Modal, extended with confirmTone='error' for the dangerous-action confirm button.
deviations_from_plan: HomeScreen (book-creation) removed rather than kept: its heading/intro chrome moved to LibraryScreen (the natural owner of the list), and the create affordance became CreateBookEntry. No dead code left behind.
useBooks() landed in brain/hooks.ts (a generic book-list view) rather than inside the feature, since it is a pure read of the SSOT reusable by future consumers (e.g. cloud-sync).

test_coverage.unit: BookService.deleteBook (persist-before-emit, isolation, unknown-book no-op) + book-library integration (list/open/confirm-cancel/confirm-delete) via App

iterations_log.label: iteration-1
architecture_choices: Two new SSOT mutations on BookService (KR-004): renameBook (trims, rejects a blank name, persist → book:updated) and duplicateBook (deep copy with a fresh book id + fresh node/edge ids; edge endpoints remapped via an id Map so references stay by stable id and point at the COPY, KR-003; « (copie) » title; persist → book:created so the live list shows it).

New brain book:updated event wired into BOTH useBooks' BOOK_LIST_EVENTS (a rename re-reads the list) and useOpenBook's BOOK_MUTATION_EVENTS (a rename reflects in an open editor) — the list stays a VIEW, no private mirror (KR-020/013/071).

BookCard gained richer meta computed inline from the book — écrans (nodes) · liens (edges) · fins (effectiveKind === 'fin', consistent with the FIN badge logic KR-054/068) — plus « Modifié le {date} » via a feature-local pure formatDate (UTC date-portion parse, timezone-stable, no Date locale dependency).

Hover-reveal actions (rename ✎ / duplicate ⧉ / delete ✕) via a CSS-only .book-card:hover/.focus-within rule (the canonical hover-reveal pattern, no isHovered JS state; revealed on keyboard focus too for a11y). Rename is in place: the title becomes an input (local edit state, KR-013) committing on Enter/blur, Esc cancels; a blank rename is a no-op (BookService rejects it too).
deviations_from_plan: « hover-reveal delete » generalised to all three card actions (rename/duplicate/delete) sharing one reveal rule — the wireframe groups them in the card corner.
Date formatting kept feature-local (book-library/utils/formatDate) since no second consumer exists yet; promote to brain/utils when cloud-sync's per-book status needs it (KR-110).

Post-review fixes (tech-lead): duplicateBook now DEEP-clones each node (JSON round-trip — structuredClone is undefined in the jsdom test env) so the copy shares no nested sub-object reference with the source (BUG-002); added an Escape-cancel rename test (BUG-003); tightened the rename no-op comparison to book.title.trim().

test_coverage.unit: BookService.renameBook (trim + book:updated, blank/missing rejection) + duplicateBook (fresh ids, remapped edges, (copie) title, book:created, independence) + book-library integration (meta counts, rename in place, duplicate adds a card)

iterations_log.label: iteration-2
architecture_choices: Search + sort are pure derived views over the live useBooks list (KR-013): a trimmed lowercased needle filters by title, then a COPY is sorted ('recent' = updatedAt desc, 'alpha' = title localeCompare 'fr'). The snapshot array from useBooks is never mutated in place (sort a copy) so the cached external-store reference stays stable. Query + sort mode are local UI state, not useEffect mirrors.

The sort control is the shared brain SegmentedControl (radiogroup, KR-117-style closed option set) and the search box the brain Field — no bespoke inputs. The toolbar only renders when the library is non-empty (nothing to search/sort otherwise).

Two distinct empty surfaces: a dashed « bibliothèque est vide » note (role=note) when there are zero books (the inviting empty state, alongside the always-present create affordance KR-072), and a « aucun livre ne correspond » status line when a search matches nothing — never a blank void.

Currently-open-book delete guard (KR-071) lives at the COMPOSITION ROOT (App), not in book-library: an App-level subscription to book:deleted reads the router route FRESH in the handler and navigates home if the deleted id is the one open in the editor — so no feature owns cross-route navigation and there is no stale-closure route dependency (KR-013). Defensive against any future delete surface, not just the library.
deviations_from_plan: The delete guard is wired even though no in-editor delete path exists yet (the library is the only delete surface, shown on the home route): it is a cheap, composition-root safety net so any future surface (or a duplicate/relink interaction) cannot strand the editor on a removed book.
The « empty state illustration » is a low-fi dashed panel with a placeholder glyph (❏) + copy, not real art — consistent with the wireframe fidelity; the glyph swaps at the icon reskin.

test_coverage.unit: book-library integration via App: search filters the grid + no-match message; default recent vs toggled alpha ordering (deterministic via a fixed system clock); empty-state note + create affordance + no toolbar when empty; delete-guard navigates home when the open book is deleted (KR-071)

iterations_log.label: iteration-3 (per-book cloud-sync status)
architecture_choices: Per-book sync chip on each card — « ✓ à jour » / « ⏳ en attente » / « ⚠ non synchronisé », hidden in a local-only build (offline = no transport, no cloud state to reflect). A live VIEW over CloudSyncService (KR-095), never a private mirror.

CloudSyncService gained a GENERIC pendingKeys(): string[] (the queued storage keys); the decorator stays book-agnostic (KR-094 — it never resolves bookKey here). The book→key mapping lives in a new brain useBookPending(bookId) hook (bookKey(id) ∈ pendingKeys), an external-store read over sync:status (KR-013), re-read on the same cadence as the global indicator (no extra events, KR-095).

The chip's (status, pending) → {label, tone} mapping is a small pure helper in BookCard (offline → null), derived once — not an ad-hoc branch ladder. « à jour » is a QUIET muted resting state (not the global pill's good/green, to avoid shouting on every card); « en attente » = accent, « non synchronisé » = bad. error/syncing are store-global while pending is per-book, so the mapping is conservative (never falsely « à jour », batch-atomic KR-095).
deviations_from_plan: Built the book-library-owned part — « reflect sync:status per book ». The other two iter-3 sub-goals need NEW CloudTransport capabilities and are deferred to a cloud-sync iteration: « reconcile the list » needs a transport list/enumerate-pull (to surface cloud-only books), and « queue deletes when offline » needs the decorator's remove() to propagate a deletion (CloudTransport has push/pull only, no delete). Both are cloud-sync's domain, not the library view's.
Existing library tests are unaffected: createBrain() has no transport (offline) so the chip renders nothing; the new chip is exercised with a transport-configured brain.

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService.pendingKeys (lists queued keys, clears on confirm, empty with no transport)
test_coverage.integration: book-library via App with a transport: a queued book shows « en attente », a confirmed book shows « à jour », a local-only build shows no chip (queries scoped to the card glyph text to avoid colliding with the global SyncIndicator)

open_questions: cloud-sync iteration: list reconciliation (pull cloud-only books — needs a CloudTransport list/enumerate) + offline DELETE propagation (decorator remove() pushing a tombstone — needs CloudTransport delete). Both deferred from book-library iter 3 as transport-capability work.
